title: P0 hosted API streaming entropy after-action
content:
Summary:

On 2028-05-14 03:21 UTC we observed a P0 degradation of the Hosted API streaming surface. Symptoms included: elevated streaming tail latency, partial chunk drops (clients observing truncated streams), and a spike of 502/504 answers for streaming requests. The incident lasted ~2h45m for the majority of traffic, with residual elevated error-rate for another 3 hours as mitigations rolled out.

Customer impact:
- ~12% of active streaming sessions experienced either truncated streams (client saw stream stop without final event) or immediate 5xx within 5s.
- Non-streaming generation endpoints were largely unaffected.
- No data loss in customer payloads was detected; however several high-SLA customers reported user-visible failures.

How we detected it:
- First alert: streaming_e2e_tail_latency_p99 fired at 2028-05-14 03:23 UTC (Ops channel).
- Secondary signal: spike in edge 5xx from streaming route (edge-proxy logs) at 03:25 UTC.
- Pager duty escalation at 03:28 UTC.

Timeline (UTC):
- 03:15 - Canary deploy of serving-runtime rev r2028-05-14a with "streaming-multiplex-optimizer" flag ON in canary zone (changes intended to reduce per-connection CPU).
- 03:20 - Canary metrics nominal.
- 03:21 - First manual traffic shift to new canary (10% traffic).
- 03:23 - streaming_e2e_tail_latency_p99 alert triggered.
- 03:25 - Edge 5xx spike observed, SREs begin triage.
- 03:33 - Identified correlation between canary allocation and increased error-rate.
- 03:36 - Rollback initiated for the new runtime in canary.
- 03:41 - Rollback completes; canary errors drop but production still showing elevated errors.
- 03:50 - Realized control-plane routing had promoted a subset of production hosts with the new binary due to a race in the rollout orchestration; SRE begins full rollback/evacuation.
- 04:05 - Evacuation and forced drain of impacted hosts in progress.
- 04:38 - Streaming error-rate back to baseline for 80% of traffic.
- 05:05 - Final impacted hosts drained and replaced; monitoring shows restoration to normal for all zones.
- 06:00 - Post-incident checks complete; gradual re-enable of canary strategy with additional guards.

Root cause (short):
A logic bug in the new "streaming-multiplex-optimizer" caused sequence IDs used to correlate streaming frames to sessions to wrap incorrectly under a rare traffic pattern (high fan-out with small token bursts). The bug manifested as session-entanglement: frames for different sessions were occasionally attributed to the wrong session id, causing the per-session reassembly code to abort and return a 502/stream-termination. Two systemic factors amplified impact: rollout orchestration raced and promoted the binary to more hosts than intended, and a KV-cache eviction storm increased CPU jitter making the buggy path more likely to trigger.

Why the bug happened (detailed):
- The optimizer introduced an abbreviated sequence ID (16-bit) to reduce memory footprint when multiplexing many simultaneous streams. Under normal load the wrap-around was extremely rare; however, a client workload with many short-lived streams and high connection churn caused hotspots where the 16-bit counter wrapped within O(1s) for a host.
- Sequence wrap-handling code assumed that wrapped IDs would be resolved by comparing timestamps, but when the reassembly queue was backpressured (due to KV-cache evictions and scheduling jitter) the timestamp comparison failed and the frame was attributed to an active session incorrectly. That triggered safety checks which aborted the session.
- Rollout control: the orchestration service had a bug in its canary promotion backoff. A transient metric spike erroneously satisfied a heuristic and the system promoted the canary from 10% to ~45% of prod in ~14 minutes instead of waiting the configured 2 hours.

Contributing factors:
- New 16-bit sequence ID optimization introduced for memory savings without sufficient stress testing for extreme churn patterns.
- KV-cache eviction policy had a configuration change earlier that week which caused heavy eviction under small-payload workloads; this increased scheduling jitter on affected hosts and made the race more likely.
- Rollout orchestration rollback/backoff heuristic was insufficiently conservative and allowed faster promotion on noisy signals.
- Monitoring/alerts: we had p99 tail latency alerting but not a small-window sudden-wrap detection metric (no metric for per-host seq-id wrap rate).

Immediate mitigation and resolution actions taken:
- 03:36 - Began rollback of the canary binary; reverted to previous stable runtime in canary hosts.
- 03:41 - Detected partial promotion; paused all automated promotions and started manual host-level reconciliation.
- 03:50 - Drained impacted hosts (forced connection drain) and redeployed stable binary.
- 04:00 - Tuned KV-cache eviction thresholds on affected host-pools to reduce reclaims and CPU jitter (short-term tweak).
- 04:30 - Re-enabled routing once 80% of traffic in each zone reported healthy streaming reassembly and p99 tail latency back within SLA.
- 05:05 - Completed full redeploy; confirmed via synthetic streaming clients and customer checks.

Longer-term mitigations (action items):
1) Replace 16-bit sequence id with 64-bit monotonic session sequence and add explicit wrap counters (owner: Marco Li, due: 2028-06-02).
2) Add canary safety gate: immutable minimum canary dwell time of 2 hours before any automated promotion beyond configured stage increments, and require at least two independent stable metrics to approve (owner: Priya Menon, due: 2028-05-28).
3) Add per-host seq-wrap-rate telemetry and alerting (new metric streaming.seq_wraps_per_min) and dashboard (owner: Devon O'Neil, due: 2028-05-24).
4) Revert the memory-optimized code-path behind a feature-flag and gate with a heavy churn stress test in our CI harness (owner: Marco Li, due: 2028-05-21).
5) Re-evaluate KV-cache eviction policy: roll forward a staged config change that increases soft-limits and adds adaptive backoff on high churn workloads (owner: SRE infra, contact: Carlos Mendes, due: 2028-05-30).
6) Update streaming runbook: include an explicit "sequence-wrap" troubleshooting section with diagnostic queries and a one-click rollback play (owner: Eng Docs, owner2: Aisha Patel, due: 2028-05-20).
7) Postdeploy canary chaos test: schedule a nightly small-burst churn test for canary clusters to detect sequence wrap pathologies early (owner: release-engineering, due: 2028-06-07).

Runbook / monitoring changes (short list):
- New alerts: streaming.seq_wrap_rate_p95 > 0 (yellow), > 5/min (pager).
- Synthetic probe changes: add 1s-burst-churn probe that opens thousands of short streams over 30s to canary pools.
- Add dashboard panel showing "seq-id-space utilization" per host and per-binary-version.

Post-incident notes for on-call teams:
- Triage flow: if streaming p99 tail climbs with correlated edge-5xx, immediately query per-host seq_wrap_rate. If seq wraps > 1/min, start canary isolation early and consider forced drain of suspect hosts.
- Use shortcut queries (examples):
  - nginx-edge logs: count of streaming 5xx by host in last 5m.
  - runtime debug counter: streaming.seq_wraps_total{bin_version} by host.
  - backlog metrics: streaming.reassembly_queue_time_p99.
- If automation promoted a canary unexpectedly, pause orchestration and escalate to release-engineering lead.

Postmortem action owners and status (short):
- Marco Li: revert/flag optimization + code change (In progress).
- Priya Menon: canary policy hardening (Planned).
- Devon O'Neil: telemetry and dashboard (In progress).
- Carlos Mendes (SRE infra): KV-cache config roll plan (Planned).
- Eng Docs / Aisha Patel: runbook updates and playbook steps (In progress).

Lessons learned / takeaways:
- Micro-optimizations (16-bit counters) can introduce correctness failure modes under real-world churn; always pair such changes with churn-focused stress tests.
- Rollout heuristics must be conservative in the presence of noisy metrics; require multiple independent signals and minimum dwell times.
- Observability gaps (missing seq-wrap metric) made root cause identification slower than necessary.
- The interplay between config (KV-cache) and code changes can create emergent failure modes—test config permutations under the CI stress harness.

Appendix (diagnostics snippets):
- Example query to find suspect hosts (PromQL-like):
  sum by (host) (increase(streaming_seq_wraps_total{bin_version="r2028-05-14a"}[5m]))

- Edge log sample (abbreviated):
  2028-05-14T03:25:11Z edge-34 stream_id=0x1fa2 err=stream-terminated reason=reassembly-failed

- Runtime debug sample:
  host=runtime-12 bin=r2028-05-14a seq_wraps_total=173 reassembly_q_len_p99=420ms

Follow-up: owners should update status in this doc as items progress. We will schedule a post-implementation verification window (2 weeks after fixes) and run the churn probe against canary and staging before re-enabling the optimization flag.

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (on-call SRE), 2028-05-16
